critical.issue: services.transfer_receipt_service.receive() calls _land() BEFORE validating note length. The 400 HTTPException is raised AFTER the CAS already flipped roll status to 'damaged' at destination. The 400 then prevents the subsequent _exception() call, leaving the roll damaged at dest with NO 'damaged' exception recorded. Observable: roll_02d43888dd4d went in_transit_transfer → damaged at wh_594ea5facd0a despite API returning 400. Also, the inventory_movement 'transfer_in' with receipt_outcome='damaged' DID insert.

critical_code_review_comments: transfer_receipt_service.receive(): the damaged-note validation happens inside the per-line loop AFTER _land(). rca of the issue: BUG — damaged outcome short-note mutates state despite 400. Root cause: services/transfer_receipt_service.py:receive() per-line order is `kind='damaged'` → viol check → `_land()` (mutates DB) → only AFTER landing does the code call `_reason(ln.note,'Keterangan kerusakan')` for the exception record, which raises HTTPException(400). HTTPException propagates out and short-circuits remaining lines, but the already-performed CAS update + inventory_movement insert are not reverted. Repro: POST /api/transfers/{dispatched_tid}/receive with lines=[{roll_id:<in_transit>,outcome:'damaged',note:'x'}] → 400. Then GET inventory_rolls/<id> shows status=damaged at dest warehouse and NO 'damaged' exception on the transfer. Mitigation: (a) hoist `if ln.outcome=='damaged': _reason(ln.note,'Keterangan kerusakan')` to the TOP of the per-line iteration, OR (b) add a Pydantic validator on TransferReceiveLine (if outcome=='damaged' then len(note.strip())>=5). Option (b) is strongest since it rejects malformed payloads at the FastAPI boundary before any business logic runs.
